ai.literal: Equity called one thing is good indeed, by the divisions having taken the proper side to behave if achieved.
ai.translation: That one quality called equity is truly good, provided one can conduct oneself justly toward every division of people.
ai.modern: பகைவர், அயலார், நண்பர் என அனைவரிடமும் அவரவர்க்கு உரிய நீதியோடு நடுவுநிலைமை தவறாமல் நடந்துகொள்ள முடிந்தால், தகுதி என்று சொல்லப்படும் அந்த ஒரு குணமே மிகவும் நல்லதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes the supreme value of impartiality, referred to here as 'takuti' (equity or fitness). It states that this single quality is inherently good. The condition for this goodness is expressed in the second line: one must manage to behave ('oḻuka peṟiṉ') by taking the proper side ('pāṟpaṭṭu') according to the different divisions of people ('pakutiyāl'). In this context, 'pakuti' refers to the natural divisions of people in one's life, such as friends, enemies, and strangers, and true equity means treating each group with the same unwavering justice.

ai.literal: Impartiality he-who-possesses's prosperity, destruction without, to descendants protection it-has.
ai.translation: The prosperity of a man of impartial justice will never perish, but will serve as a secure protection for his descendants.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமை உடையவனுடைய செல்வமானது அழிவில்லாமல் அவனுடைய சந்ததியினருக்கும் பாதுகாப்பாக அமையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring nature of wealth earned through fairness. The word 'ceppam' refers to rectitude or impartiality. While ill-gotten wealth might seem to grow, the prosperity ('ākkam') of a just person is unique because it suffers no destruction ('citaivu iṉṟi'). Instead, it leaves a lasting legacy, providing security ('ēmāppu') to their descendants ('eccam', literally 'that which is left behind').

ai.literal: Good indeed even if it yields, impartiality having deviated which accrues wealth, that very day to cease let one abandon.
ai.translation: Even if it brings great good, abandon immediately any wealth gained by departing from impartiality.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமையிலிருந்து தவறி வரும் செல்வமானது நன்மையே தருவதாக இருந்தாலும், அதனை அப்போதே கைவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the temptation of ill-gotten gains. Even if wealth acquired by compromising one's fairness seems to offer immense benefits, it should be rejected outright. True equity requires discarding any advantage that comes at the cost of justice, on the very day it appears.

ai.literal: Worthy people, worthiness they are without, that which is said, by their respective remainders to be seen will be.
ai.translation: Whether people are just or unjust will be seen by what they leave behind.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் நடுவுநிலைமை உடையவரா அல்லது இல்லாதவரா என்பது, அவர் தமக்குப்பின் விட்டுச்செல்லும் எச்சத்தால் அறியப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how to judge a person's true character and impartiality. The word 'தக்கார்' refers to those who are worthy and just, while 'தகவிலர்' refers to those lacking such equity. The key word 'எச்சம்' means 'remainder' or 'what is left behind', which can be understood as their legacy, reputation, or offspring. Ultimately, whether a person was truly impartial is revealed to the world by the lasting impact and legacy they leave after their time.

ai.literal: Ruin and increase non-existent are not; of the mind unbending to the noble ones is ornament.
ai.translation: Loss and gain are not uncommon in life. To remain unbending in mind through them is the true ornament of the noble.
ai.modern: வாழ்வில் அழிவும் பெருக்கமும் இல்லாதவை அல்ல, அவை இயற்கையே. ஆனால் அந்த நிலைகளிலும் மனம் கோணாமல் நடுநிலையோடு இருப்பதே சான்றோர்களுக்கு அழகாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet observes that loss and gain are inevitable parts of human life. The phrase 'il alla' emphasizes that these fluctuations are not non-existent, meaning they happen to everyone. The true mark of nobility, therefore, is 'kōṭāmai'—the unbending impartiality of the mind. Maintaining this steady, unbiased state regardless of changing fortunes is described as the greatest ornament for the wise.

ai.literal: "I will perish" that-fact let-him-know, one's-own heart impartiality having-abandoned wrong-things if-does.
ai.translation: If one's own heart abandons impartiality and does wrong, let him know that he will perish.
ai.modern: தன் நெஞ்சம் நடுவுநிலைமையை விட்டு விலகித் தவறான செயல்களைச் செய்தால், தான் கெட்டுப்போவோம் என்பதை ஒருவன் அறிந்துகொள்ள வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the inevitable ruin that follows the loss of impartiality. The phrase 'தன் நெஞ்சம்' (one's own heart) emphasizes that the individual is fully aware of their own deviation from fairness. 'நடுவு ஒரீஇ அல்ல செயின்' describes the act of abandoning the middle path to commit unjust deeds. When this happens, the person should realize 'கெடுவல் யான்' (I will perish), as moral destruction is certain.

ai.literal: as ruin will not consider the world being impartial in goodness he who abides decline
ai.translation: The world will not consider as ruin the decline of a person who abides in goodness and maintains impartiality.
ai.modern: நடுவுநிலைமையோடு அறத்தில் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் ஒருவருக்கு ஏற்படும் வறுமையை உலகம் ஒரு கேடாகக் கருதாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how society views the material decline of a truly just person. The word 'தாழ்வு' means a lowering of status or wealth, while 'கெடு' means absolute ruin or destruction. The world does not see the poverty of someone who remains impartial and rooted in goodness as a true loss. Instead, their enduring virtue is recognized as their true wealth, making their material decline insignificant.

ai.literal: Equal having made, which weighs scale like, having been set, to one side not leaning, to the noble ones ornament.
ai.translation: To rest level and not lean to one side, like a well-calibrated balance scale, is the true ornament of the noble.
ai.modern: முதலில் தன்னைச் சமமாக நிறுத்திக்கொண்டு, பின்பு பொருளின் எடையைச் சரியாகக் காட்டும் தராசுகோல் போல, நடுவுநிலைமையோடு அமைந்து ஒரு பக்கமாகச் சாயாமல் இருப்பதே சான்றோர்க்கு அழகாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares an impartial person to a balance scale. A good scale first rests perfectly level ('சமன் செய்து') and then accurately weighs what is placed on it ('சீர்தூக்கும் கோல்') without leaning unfairly to one side ('ஒருபால் கோடாமை'). In the same way, a noble person must first be grounded in equity and then judge situations without bias. This unwavering impartiality is described as the true ornament ('அணி') that adorns the wise and noble ('சான்றோர்').

ai.literal: Speech-crookedness that-which-is-without (is) uprightness, firmly inner-crookedness absence if-obtained.
ai.translation: Uprightness is speech without bias, provided one has firmly attained the absence of bias in the mind.
ai.modern: உள்ளத்தில் உறுதியாக எந்த ஒரு சார்பும் இல்லாத தன்மையைப் பெற்றிருந்தால், சொல்லிலும் சார்பு இல்லாமல் இருப்பதே உண்மையான நடுவுநிலைமை ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true impartiality (செப்பம்). It states that uprightness is the absence of bias or crookedness in one's speech (சொற்கோட்டம் இல்லது). However, this is only valid if one has firmly secured the absence of bias in one's mind (உட்கோட்டம் இன்மை பெறின்). The contrasting words 'சொற்கோட்டம்' (crookedness in speech) and 'உட்கோட்டம்' (crookedness in mind) emphasize that fair speech must stem from a genuinely fair mind.

ai.literal: Trade to those who do trade having protected others' things also one's own things like if they do.
ai.translation: True trade for those who trade is to protect others' goods and treat them as their own.
ai.modern: பிறர் பொருளையும் தம்முடைய பொருளைப் போலப் பாதுகாத்து வியாபாரம் செய்தால் அதுவே வியாபாரம் செய்பவர்களுக்குச் சிறந்த வியாபாரம் ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the core of ethical business. The word vaanikam is used twice: first to mean the act of trading, and second to mean the true spirit of trade. The key to this true trade is peeni (protecting or caring for) others' goods (piravum) exactly as one would care for one's own (tama pool). By treating the buyer's or partner's interests with the same care as their own, a trader upholds perfect impartiality.
